Your armband on Haaland looks sound. He's marginally ahead of Salah and has genuine upside—a quarter chance of double figures—against a small tail risk. Hold that.

The transfer to Watkins gains 6.4 points across the horizon with no hit cost, so it's a clear win. Wood out, Watkins in.

Your main concentration is Arsenal: three players in the starting eleven. That's a structural choice you've made and it's defensible—Raya, Gabriel and Saka all project well—but worth knowing. Liverpool's two (Salah and Van Dijk) and Manchester City's two (Gvardiol and Haaland) are less dense. Your bench is thin; Mykolenko at 3.1 is the only real alternative if someone doesn't play.

The model has been cautious of late—seven of its last eleven calls were wrong—so don't treat these projections as certainty. That said, nothing here looks badly misaligned. Make the Wood swap and play as is.

Your team projects 69.0 this week with Haaland captained. That's a clean setup: Haaland is 0.3 clear of Salah and carries genuine upside (25% chance of 10+), though he also has tail risk. The captain choice is tight enough that you'd only swap it if Salah were flagged, which he isn't.

The Wood-to-Watkins swap makes sense over the horizon at a cost of no hits, and you'll have a free transfer banked next week. Wood projects only 4.2 and Watkins is a direct upgrade. You're not forced to move him this week, but the numbers support it if you want to act.

Arsenal and Liverpool dominate your midfield—three and two players respectively. That's heavy, but their projections are simply the strongest. Your bench is thin; if you needed to reshuffle for injury or rotation, Mykolenko is your only meaningful option there.

The model has been underwater in this format, so any week near or above projection is a win. Proceed with confidence in the Watkins transfer if it suits your longer view; otherwise, a held chip week is fine too.

Your eleven projects 69.0 with the armband on Haaland, who is a narrow favourite over Salah—only 0.3 clear—but has the higher ceiling at 25% for double figures. Salah at 7.9 is close enough that you would not regret either choice, though Haaland carries more variance.

The transfer Wood to Watkins gains 6.4 points at no hit cost, and the model favours it cleanly. Watkins is the stronger projection of the two. You have the funds and the space.

Your bench is thin: Mykolenko alone projects above 3, and the starter list leaves little to hope for if someone fails to play. That is the trade-off you have accepted with this shape and these picks. The engine has underperformed by 13 points across 11 decisions, which is worth noting if the model's logic ever feels alien—it is fallible—but this week's advice sits on firmer ground than average.

Make the transfer and play as you have lined up.
